title: AWS Agent Registry
hook: A governed org-wide catalog of agents, tools, skills, and MCP servers — with owners on record.

kv.v: Ownership, supported protocols, capabilities, and invocation details for each entry.
Shadow-agent sprawl is a governance risk more mundane than prompt injection — and arguably more dangerous.

back.hookline: The 'service catalog' moment for agents: if it's not in the registry, it doesn't officially exist.

product_name_lead.template: As deployments scale from a handful of agents to hundreds, nobody knows what exists, who owns it, or whether it was approved. AWS Agent Registry (preview via AgentCore) is a governed catalogue for discovering, sharing, and reusing agents, tools, skills, and MCP servers across an organization.

product_name_lead.unresolvable_reason: Prose containing the product name. The rename itself is deterministic, but rewriting a sentence is authorship, and the new name contains the old one so substitution is not safely repeatable. Tier C, with the original retained.

review_reasons.reason: Tier C prose substitution of a renamed product name (product_name_lead), applied by an agent. Needs human sign-off; the Tier A rename of the title itself is deterministic and does not.

history.reason: Mechanical migration from agentcore-flashcards.html; card text lifted verbatim from the legacy DECK literal.

August 2026 release notes: "AWS Agent Registry launches under the new `agent-registry` namespace" (matched on regis). Corroborated by agentcore.feature-regions, which uses the same name verbatim. Old name retained in aka[] so search and shared links keep resolving. The entry also announces the "agent-registry" namespace; the card's service key is deliberately NOT repointed, because the pinned API surface still carries this feature's operations under bedrock-agentcore-control.
